subject: Information Theory
title: OFDM: Dividing the Spectrum
description: A quick win: understand OFDM: Dividing the Spectrum.

hook.text: Wi-Fi sends data on dozens of tiny sub-channels at once. If one is jammed, the others carry on.

buildup.text: OFDM splits a wide channel into many narrow orthogonal sub-carriers, each carrying a small piece of data.

discovery.text: Orthogonality means sub-carriers don't interfere with each other despite overlapping in frequency.

twist.text: OFDM turns one difficult wideband channel into many easy narrowband channels. Each can be independently optimized.

climax.text: 4G, 5G, Wi-Fi, and digital TV all use OFDM. It's the dominant modulation scheme of the modern era.

punchline.text: Many narrow lanes beat one wide highway.

quiz.question: What does OFDM do?
options: Splits a wide channel into many narrow sub-carriers
